guided_plan.optimized_prompt:
You are writing an Amazon US product listing for a cotton tote bag in natural, plain US English. Use only the confirmed product facts supplied in {{PRODUCT_FACTS}}; treat any fact marked unknown or missing as unavailable and do not state, estimate, or imply it. Use {{KEYWORDS}} only as candidate search terms: include a term only when the confirmed facts support it, and drop any term that would require an unverified claim.

Deliver four parts:
1. Title: lead with what the item is (cotton tote bag), then the most useful confirmed attributes such as material, fabric weight, dimensions, capacity, and handle/carry style. Keep it readable, avoid keyword stuffing and repeated numbers, and stay within the current Amazon US title length limit defined in the rule pack supplied at use time.
2. item_highlights: a short set of scannable phrases, each conveying one distinct confirmed benefit or spec, within the current item_highlights length limit in the rule pack supplied at use time.
3. bullet_points: each bullet starts with a short capitalized benefit label, then one or two sentences explaining a single confirmed feature and why a shopper cares (for example how the size or handle length affects everyday carrying). Give each bullet a stable ID. Do not repeat the same spec across multiple bullets; spread material, size, capacity, handle/carry style, and label/rebranding details so each bullet adds new information.
4. description: a short paragraph or two in plain prose that summarizes the confirmed facts and typical use context, without restating every number already in the bullets.

Hard rules:
- Do not invent or imply certifications, eco-friendly/biodegradable/compostable/recycled claims, antimicrobial or health claims, load ratings, durability test results, color, pack quantity, brand, or country of origin unless they appear as confirmed in {{PRODUCT_FACTS}}.
- Do not include prices, promotions, shipping offers, availability, seller contact details, URLs, or company-specific information.

- Output only the listing copy; do not add notes about missing data in the customer-facing text.

You are writing an Amazon US product listing for a cotton tote bag in natural, plain US English. Use only the confirmed product facts supplied in {{PRODUCT_FACTS}}; treat any fact marked unknown or missing as unavailable and do not state, estimate, or imply it. Use {{KEYWORDS}} only as candidate search terms: include a term only when the confirmed facts support it, and drop any term that would require an unverified claim.

Deliver four parts:
1. Title: lead with what the item is (cotton tote bag), then the most useful confirmed attributes such as material, fabric weight, dimensions, capacity, and handle/carry style. Keep it readable, avoid keyword stuffing and repeated numbers, and stay within the current Amazon US title length limit defined in the rule pack supplied at use time.
2. item_highlights: a short set of scannable phrases, each conveying one distinct confirmed benefit or spec, within the current item_highlights length limit in the rule pack supplied at use time.
3. bullet_points: each bullet starts with a short capitalized benefit label, then one or two sentences explaining a single confirmed feature and why a shopper cares (for example how the size or handle length affects everyday carrying). Give each bullet a stable ID. Do not repeat the same spec across multiple bullets; spread material, size, capacity, handle/carry style, and label/rebranding details so each bullet adds new information.
4. description: a short paragraph or two in plain prose that summarizes the confirmed facts and typical use context, without restating every number already in the bullets.

Hard rules:
- Do not invent or imply certifications, eco-friendly/biodegradable/compostable/recycled claims, antimicrobial or health claims, load ratings, durability test results, color, pack quantity, brand, or country of origin unless they appear as confirmed in {{PRODUCT_FACTS}}.
- Do not include prices, promotions, shipping offers, availability, seller contact details, URLs, or company-specific information.
- Keep units and attributes distinct: capacity in volume, fabric weight in gsm, dimensions in length units; never convert one attribute into another.
- If a fact needed for a keyword or claim is missing, omit the claim rather than filling the gap.
- Output only the listing copy; do not add notes about missing data in the customer-facing text.
